## 1. A quantitative limitation on degradable-extension converses

I derived a positive capacity floor for **every degradable extension of the fixed single-use channel**, with arbitrary separable receiver and environment spaces.

Let \(M\) be degradable, with the same one-mode input and photon-number observable as \(\mathcal N_x\), and suppose
\[
\mathcal N_x=L\circ M
\]
for some receiver postprocessing \(L\). For \(x<1/2\), choose a finite integer \(J\) such that
\[
c_{J,x}
=
1-\left(1+\frac{J}{1+x}\right)
  \left(\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^J
>
\frac12+x.
\]
Define
\[
G_{J,x}=2c_{J,x}(2c_{J,x}-1-2x),
\qquad
w_{J,x}
=
\frac{G_{J,x}}{8J+16c_{J,x}\sqrt J}.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
Q_E(M)\ge
\min\{1,2E\}\,
\frac{w_{J,x}^{\,2}}{9\ln2}>0 .
}
\]

**This lower-bounds the extension’s capacity, not the capacity of \(\mathcal N_x\).** Capacity can decrease strictly under \(L\).

### Why this holds

The governing primary ingredient is the universal recovery theorem of Junge–Renner–Sutter–Wilde–Winter, used with its separable-space and support conditions. It supplies one recovery map shared by a family of input states and exactly recovers their average. The quantitative channel conversion below is derived in this return. [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.07127?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Restrict \(M\)’s input to \(\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle\}\), and put
\[
q=I_c(I/2,M)
\]
in bits. Apply the recovery theorem to the six pure Pauli eigenstates and the degrading map \(M\to M^c\). Their relative-entropy losses sum to \(6q\). Because each probe output is bounded above by twice the average output, these relative entropies are finite even when individual output entropies are infinite.

The common recovery map \(\mathcal R\) satisfies
\[
\|M-\mathcal R M^c\|_\diamond
\le 6\sqrt{(\ln2)q}.
\]
This includes arbitrary untouched references and has no output-dimension factor.

The actual receiver branch and the recovered complementary branch form a joint channel. Symmetrizing them produces an antidegradable channel, giving
\[
\operatorname{dist}_\diamond
\bigl(\mathcal N_x|_{\{0,1\}},\mathrm{AD}\bigr)
\le 3\sqrt{(\ln2)q}.
\]
The accepted bounded quadrature witness supplies the lower bound \(w_{J,x}\) on this distance. Combining the two inequalities and padding active qubit inputs with vacuum proves the displayed capacity floor.
